The first m coordinates of Πg have density qm  Dg(b) − P a≤m(x2 a − ℓa)  q(Dg(b)) Y a≤m e−x2 a/(2ℓa) √ 2πℓa . (2.5) These consistent densities are measurable in g and independent of b. For each fixed 0 ≤ j < ∞, Πg[|xa|j] ≤ Cj,g,bℓ j/2 a , with a finite constant uniform in a. For sufficiently large fixed m, the tail beyond m has a density bounded by a finite constant relative to N a>m N(0, ℓa). Conditional on that tail, the first m coordinates have the Gaussian angular law on the sphere of squared radius Dg(b) + X a≤m ℓa − X a>m (x2 a − ℓa). In particular the renormalized constraint holds Πg-almost surely. These are the statements of [22, Proposition 2.3]. 2. With bn = 1 + (−g1,n)+ and b = 1 + (−g1)+, the spherical and cube edge marginals converge jointly with the edge points to Πg on the represented subsequences described below. Cube integrals converge for every continuous cylinder of polynomial growth. Spherical coordinates obey the uniform bounds µsp [|xa|j ] ≤ Cj(ga,n + bn)−j/2 , lim m→∞ sup n X a>m (ga,n + bn)−2 = 0 after discarding finitely many n on such a representation. Here µsp is surface measure on {|σ|2 = n}, tilted by exp(σTWσ/2). The sources are [22, Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 3.3]. 7 3. The Euclidean gradient on smooth compact cylinders is closable from L2(Πg) to L2(Πg; ℓ2). The associated closed form has kernel equal to the constants. Every coordinate belongs to its domain and satisfies ∇xa = ea, hence Eg(xa) = 1. This is [22, Proposition 5.1]. The usual contraction rule for gradients passes to the closure, so the form is Dirichlet and Sg t is a conservative symmetric Markov semigroup. 4. On a quenched represented subsequence, say that fn converges weakly to F ∈ L2(Πg) if its L2(µ) norms are bounded and µ[fnϕ(x)] → Πg[Fϕ] for every smooth compact cylinder ϕ; call the convergence strong when in addition µ[f2 n] → Πg[F2]. Suppose, for fixed C, D < ∞, that ∥fn∥∞ ≤ CnD, that TnE(fn) is bounded, and that fn converges weakly to F. Then F belongs to the closed form domain and lim inf n TnE(fn) ≥ c∗Eg(F). (2.6) Conversely, for every smooth compact cylinder F, there are functions fn,j, polynomially bounded for each fixed j, such that fn,j converges strongly to F as n → ∞ for each j, and lim j→∞ lim n→∞ TnE(fn,j) = c∗Eg(F). (2.7) The source asserts a common represented event for countably many chosen sources and tests. Recovery is used at each fixed j, followed by the displayed j-limit [22, Theorem 6.8].
